title: The Last Light
blurb: Voxel Siege is now Last Light Keep. Every other beacon in the Ashen March has gone dark; yours is the fire the Ashen King is marching to put out.
hi: Last Light Keep, and a reason to hold it.
sec: Nothing to do: stars, skill picks and difficulty tracks carry over.
Saves keep working across the rename
The build menu, tower menu and spell bar use painted art.
Build menu: a painted badge for each tower
Upgrade, aim, rally and sell buttons
Militia Call, Catapult Barrage and Frost Nova buttons
Enemies no longer spin in place while two or more soldiers fight them.
Soldiers and militia now hold their spots around an enemy instead of circling it
Goblin Shamans keep walking while they shoot your soldiers.
They used to stop, and a pack just out of tower reach could hold a battle up forever

title: Beat of War
blurb: Phase 3 is complete. The War Drum joins the Barracks, soldiers get a full rework, and your stars finally buy something: the War Council skill tree.
hi: Militia Call, Catapult Barrage and Frost Nova.
A support tower that makes everything around it fire faster.
Stronger soldiers, real sword fights, and Overwatch for Rangers.
Eight skill trees bought with your stars.
Every difficulty earns its own three stars.
sec: Deals no damage. Every tower in its radius fires faster.
Cost 110 gold, unlocks at 3-1 Frostmere Reach
War Horn (280 gold): boosted towers also get +20% range
Hex Totem (280 gold): enemies in the radius take +15% damage from everything
A Barracks inside the radius respawns soldiers faster
Soldiers were falling behind tougher enemies. Now they hold.
A soldier that is already blocking holds one more enemy
Holy knights that refuse to stay down.
Three bows, and a new place to stand.
Overwatch: rally them off the road to shoot from safety; they never block
The road got wider, and they use all of it.
Walk anywhere across the 1.5-tile road instead of one line
Turn to face the soldier they are fighting
Two militiamen rise on the road and block for 12 s.
Aim ahead: five boulders land 3 s later.
60 per boulder in a 2-tile circle, 0.5 s stun
Freezes ground enemies within 2.5 tiles for 2.5 s; bosses are slowed 50%
Spend stars on permanent upgrades, from the Upgrades button on the world map.
Eight trees: Kingdom plus one per tower, each a different shape
Pick-one-of-two choices, including the specialisation split
Refunds are free; the tree is off in Watch mode
Tree bonuses show in the almanac and on tower cards
Casual is the new baseline. Normal and Impossible hit harder, in health and damage.
Veteran (1.3x health) is now Impossible: 1.5x health and damage
Every difficulty has its own three stars: copper, silver and gold.
First-clear bounty: +1 skill point on Normal, +3 on Impossible
Wins from before this patch count as Casual
Each level keeps its own tower set, even on a replay.
Beating later levels no longer opens every tower on earlier ones
Progress is saved to your account and survives new versions
The level card lists your towers, with New tags
Swords swing, shields bash and Paladins slam.
Wind-up, swing with a swoosh, lunge and recover
Soldiers fan out around one enemy; enemies flinch when hit
Rangers draw, release and reach for the quiver
Fallen soldiers topple; new ones march out; the squad cheers after an upgrade
All five War Drum forms, and soldiers rebuilt from their painted art.
Tap a soldier to see its name, stats and what it is doing.

title: Hold the Line
blurb: Soldiers take the field. The Barracks puts a squad on the road, and every ground enemy learns to fight back.
hi: Soldiers that block the road and fight hand to hand.
Every ground enemy can now hit your soldiers.
sec: Three soldiers guard a rally point you choose.
Paladins (260 gold): tough healers with a holy strike every 4th hit
Rangers (250 gold): archers that also hit flyers
Tap the flag button, then the road, to move the rally point
Shown per hit with hit speed, like towers.
Ogre Brute hits two soldiers at once; Gruk and the Warlord splash
Goblin Shamans strike soldiers from 3 tiles
A Boar Rider’s first block is a charge that knocks the soldier aside
A Barracks row, enemy Attack stats, and Gate damage renamed Castle damage.

title: Hard Mode Is the New Normal
blurb: Greenvale was too easy. Enemies are tougher everywhere, and the Overload stops melting bosses alone.
hi: Normal now plays like the old Veteran.
sec: Still the boss killer, just not alone.
Levels you have won never lock again when a new level is added before them.
Painted art, and 3D models rebuilt to match.
Health by wave now uses the map where the enemy first appears.

title: The Ashen March
blurb: A Kingdom Rush style campaign: a 3D world map, briefings, difficulty and levels that open one at a time.
hi: A voxel diorama with fog over unreached lands.
Four levels from the castle gates to the bog.
Sapper, Boar Rider and the boss Gruk.
sec: Pick a level, read its story, choose a difficulty.
Levels open one at a time
Towers and upgrades unlock as you progress
Millbrook Fields, River Crossing, Thornwood, Mire’s Edge.
1-1 is a tutorial with on-screen tips
Mire’s Edge: boggy road slows ground enemies to 70%
Knocks out the first tower it reaches for 5 s.
Fast, and shrugs off the first slow.
Boss. At half health two Boar Riders charge out.
One display font everywhere; the Almanac moved to the world map and battle.

title: Fresh Faces
blurb: Every enemy rebuilt in a cel-shaded style, and a painted title screen.
sec: All nine enemies rebuilt from the art board.
Painted key art, the logo, and a loading bar.

title: The Almanac
blurb: A seed-packet almanac with real numbers, and the Siege Mortar becomes the armor breaker.
hi: Every number, and how it changes by level.
sec: Less raw damage, but it cracks armor.
Tower packets, number stats, rank picker, armor and magic resist meters.

title: New Look
blurb: All five towers rebuilt from the art board.
sec: New models for Archer Tower, Cannon, Flame Tower, Frost Spire and Tesla Coil.
Siege Mortar’s blind spot shown as a red ring
Specialisation tooltips no longer repeat their numbers.

title: The Siege Begins
blurb: The playable game: five towers, specialisations, three damage types, four maps and a self-playing Watch mode.
